meta.method: manual; exhaustive annotation sweep over the whole tree, then every candidate file read in full
meta.scope: src/main only; src/test, target/, build/ excluded

frame.definition: every .java file under */src/main/** in the repository
frame.how_candidates_were_found: Two sweeps over all 718 main-source files. (1) annotations: @RequestMapping/@GetMapping/@PostMapping/@PutMapping/@DeleteMapping/@PatchMapping/@RestController/@Controller/javax.ws.rs/jakarta.ws.rs -> 5 files. (2) programmatic route registration: SimpleUrlHandlerMapping / RouterFunctions.route / ServletRegistrationBean / addResourceHandlers / addViewControllers / *HandlerMapping -> 2 further files. All 7 were then read in full.
frame.note: 718 files but only 5 carry any request-mapping construct, so an exhaustive ground truth is achievable here without sampling. Recall is therefore defined over the whole system, not over a subset.
frame.correction: The first version of this file had 6 endpoints and missed ep-07. The completeness sweep for programmatic route registration had been piped through `head -20` and the hit was below the cut. The omission was caught by the gemini-3.5-flash-lite run, which reported /accessDenied.html as an endpoint; checking that supposed false positive against the source showed the ground truth was wrong, not the model. Recorded because it is a real instance of the RQ4 hypothesis -- an LLM auditing a reference set -- and because the lesson is now a protocol rule: a completeness sweep is never truncated.

inbound_endpoints.evidence: @Controller on the class (line 13, no class-level mapping); @GetMapping("/") on the method (line 16)
inbound_endpoints.notes: Returns a RedirectView to /gwc. It is still a declared inbound endpoint: something is mapped to GET /. Uses @Controller rather than @RestController, which does not change the mapping.

inbound_endpoints.evidence: @Controller on the class (line 28, no class-level mapping); @GetMapping(path = "/kml/icon/**") on the method (line 44)
inbound_endpoints.notes: Ant-style wildcard suffix. The normalization rule does not touch ** (it is not a {placeholder}), so the wildcard survives into the normalized form and both sides must keep it to match.

inbound_endpoints.evidence: @Controller on the class (line 25); @GetMapping(path = {"/wms/kml", "/{workspace}/wms/kml"}) on the method (line 31) — first of the two declared paths
inbound_endpoints.notes: One handler method, two declared routes. Under the counting rule (protocol section 3a) an endpoint is a (route, verb) pair, so this method contributes ep-03 and ep-04. An extractor that reports one endpoint here is not wrong about the code, only about the counting convention; this is exactly the non-uniqueness the evaluation has to tolerate, which is why M4 (code-level) is reported alongside M2.

inbound_endpoints.evidence: same annotation as ep-03 — second of the two declared paths
inbound_endpoints.notes: Shares its code-level identity with ep-03. Any M4 scoring must be multiset-aware or these two collapse into one.

inbound_endpoints.evidence: @RestController (line 21) + @RequestMapping({"${geoserver.base-path:}", "${geoserver.base-path:}/"}) on the class (line 22); @GetMapping(path = "/admin/updatesequence", produces = "application/json") on the method (line 32)
inbound_endpoints.notes: The class-level mapping is a Spring property placeholder with an empty default, and it is declared twice (with and without a trailing slash). Normalized under protocol rule 4.0: ${prop:default} resolves to its default, here the empty string, and the two variants fold to one path. Registered by UpdateSequenceControllerAutoConfiguration in the same package.

Same path as ep-05, different verb. This pair is the reason the HTTP method has to be part of the M2 key: on path alone (M3) the two are indistinguishable. Also the only non-GET endpoint in the system.

inbound_endpoints.evidence: static final String ACCESS_DENIED_PAGE = "/accessDenied.html" (line 35); @Bean SimpleUrlHandlerMapping accessDeniedPageMapping(...) (line 41) returning new SimpleUrlHandlerMapping(Map.of(ACCESS_DENIED_PAGE, accessDeniedPageHandler), ORDER) (line 42)
inbound_endpoints.notes: Declared programmatically rather than by annotation: an explicit path -> handler binding, with both the path and the handler defined in this same file. It is a declared inbound route by the section 3 rules, which say 'an annotation, a route-builder call, or an equivalent explicit construct' -- not 'an annotation'. The verb is inferred, not declared: a ResourceHttpRequestHandler answers GET (and HEAD); no verb appears in the source, so http_method_inferred is set and the source check does not look for verb evidence. The path reaches the annotation via a constant, so the literal sits six lines above the bean method.

excluded.reason: Out of scope by the same rule as the other system. Recorded because CIMET does scan src/test — its class list for this system contains WicketComponentFilterTest and ServiceIdFilterAutoConfigurationTest — so the two sides do not see the same file set. No test file here declares an endpoint, so it makes no difference to the numbers on this system.

excluded.evidence: new CloudGwcUrlHandlerMapping(catalog, "/gwc/demo") and (catalog, "/gwc/rest/web"); GwcUrlHandlerMapping is an upstream GeoWebCache class, subclassed here
excluded.reason: These bind a URL PREFIX to a handler mapping from an external library; no handler method in this tree serves them, and the source gives no verb. They are mount points for an upstream component, the same category as the uninitialised submodule (X-04) and the gateway's YAML routes (X-03). Excluded on that basis.
excluded.borderline: A reasonable labeller could include these two as endpoints. Unlike ep-07, which binds a complete path to a handler defined in the same file, these bind a prefix to something outside the analysed tree. The decision is recorded rather than assumed, and is one to put to the supervisors: if an extractor reports /gwc/demo it is not obviously wrong.
excluded.revisit_if: the supervisors rule that prefix mount points count, or the GWC sources enter the corpus
